dimension_grades.evidence: The entire draft is written in narrative prose paragraphs; there are no bullet points anywhere in the update.
No bullets exist; instead, paragraphs run multiple sentences long, e.g., 'After several productive working sessions, we were able to finalize the schema redesign...'
The payment processor issue is mentioned in 'Blockers and Challenges' and again referenced in 'Next Steps,' and the CI/CD pipeline issue appears in both sections as well.
A standalone 'Broader Context' section exists that discusses hiring freeze and burnout, content that could be folded into blockers or next steps rather than warranting its own section.
The first line after the greeting is 'I hope this message finds you well and that you had a great weekend,' which is context-setting pleasantry, not a status summary.
There is no single summary sentence capturing wins and timeline shifts; wins and blockers are buried separately in different paragraphs.
No upfront summary line signals whether the reader needs to act; the escalation recommendation is buried mid-draft in the Blockers section.
There is no summary line at all, labeled or otherwise, so this dimension cannot be met.
The draft uses alarm words including 'significant setback,' 'serious concern,' 'scrambling,' 'failed,' and 'headache' to describe engineering challenges.
The draft says 'it's hard to say exactly when we'll know more' about the timeline impact, leaving it entirely vague rather than stating a concrete estimate.
No specific date or timeframe is given for when the resolution path will be clear; the draft only says they 'hope to have a clearer picture' without specifying when.
Rather than signaling no escalation is needed, the draft explicitly recommends escalation: 'I'd recommend we flag both of these to the VP sooner rather than later.'
The draft contains no internet-style abbreviations or casual shorthand labels; it errs toward formal prose throughout.

The closing reads 'Please don't hesitate to reach out if you'd like to set up time to discuss any of this in greater detail. I'm happy to put together a more comprehensive briefing document,' which is overly formal and stiff.

The draft opens with 'I hope this message finds you well' and uses verbose, formal prose throughout, showing no calibration to a director who reads on mobile between meetings and needs concise communication.
